slice.candidate: Software Heritage origin latest-visit plus snapshot branch/revision chain as a read-only independent witness for existing archive presence and source-to-revision linkage

comparison_assumptions.expected_completion_time: short: official API semantics audit plus bounded public browse-path probe
comparison_assumptions.success_probability_for_existing_origin_: high when the origin has a completed/partial visit with a snapshot
comparison_assumptions.success_probability_for_fresh_arbitrary_: low-to-medium because archive crawl freshness is not guaranteed and arbitrary historical membership may require revision-history traversal
comparison_assumptions.integration_cost: low for direct snapshot branch targets; potentially unbounded for arbitrary historical commit search
comparison_assumptions.optional_monthly_quota_fragility: no finite monthly/trial/paid quota identified for documented public GET paths; ordinary service/rate limits remain possible

public_sources.finding: GET origin/visit/latest can return the latest archived visit and, with require_snapshot, a visit carrying a snapshot identifier; the visit date is archive-visit time, not a source-freshness guarantee.
A snapshot is a full picture of an origin at collection time; named branches point directly to revision/release/other DAG objects, but the API returns branches in bounded pages.
Revision IDs are Git-compatible commit identifiers and revision/log provides GET-only ancestry traversal from a known head, with bounded limits.
The documented origin -> latest visit -> snapshot -> branch revision chain is sufficient to identify revisions directly referenced by a collected snapshot.

Public browse views expose snapshot history and branches for an origin without special permission; a live example fetch through this environment was unavailable due cache/safety routing, so no current-origin freshness claim is made.

slice.tested_scope: Official public Software Heritage origin latest-visit, snapshot, revision/log and browse-snapshot semantics plus one attempted public browse-path fetch. No O, downstream, other-worker state, legacy research, shared ledger, other-role receipt/config, private data, secret, POST/Save Code Now request, provenance special-permission endpoint, hosted runner, external executor, manual witness, finite paid quota, scheduler mutation, wait/poll/backoff, or second leaf was used.
reasoning: When origin/visit/latest returns a visit with a snapshot, the read-only chain proves that Software Heritage has an archived snapshot for that origin at the reported visit time. The snapshot can directly bind named branches to Git-compatible revision identifiers.

This does not guarantee that the latest archive visit is fresh enough to contain a newly retained source commit; the documented latest endpoint is latest relative to Software Heritage visits and gives no collection-freshness SLA.

A transaction commit intentionally kept as the direct target of a dedicated source ref would make membership cheap to check after a crawl because the snapshot branch can point directly to that revision. For an arbitrary historical commit, exact membership can require revision/log traversal from one or more branch heads and can be large/paginated; an orphaned or no-longer-reachable commit need not be linked from the latest snapshot.

Therefore the path is a useful zero-cost optional witness after independent archival has already occurred, but it is not a deterministic scheduled-Chat-only mechanism for immediate, universal, deletion-surviving witness creation without Save Code Now or an independently guaranteed crawl.

frontier: Preserve the prior single-ref immutable transaction-record plus force=false ref-update design as the current Chat-callable repository baseline.
Software Heritage existing-object lookup and origin-snapshot linkage are useful independent read-only witnesses only after archival presence already exists.
A dedicated retained source ref can make post-crawl snapshot membership O(1)-like via a direct branch target, but no read-only path guarantees crawl freshness or immediate archive presence.
